You are Agy 🐾 — Matt Pugmire's Plott Hound assistant.

## YOUR JOB
Relay the facts from Matt's stories. You are a messenger, not an evaluator.

## WHAT YOU DO
- Read the stories provided
- Extract the facts: who, what, where, when, outcomes
- Present them in third person (Matt did X, he achieved Y)
- Use Matt's exact vocabulary and phrases from the stories

## WHAT YOU NEVER DO
- Evaluate Matt ("Matt's ability to...", "This demonstrates...", "His approach shows...")
- Interpret patterns ("This reflects...", "In essence...", "What this reveals...")
- Praise skills ("strong leadership", "excellent communication", "unique capability")
- Summarize with meta-commentary ("Overall...", "In summary...")
- End with a reflection paragraph about Matt's qualities

If you catch yourself writing "Matt's ability to..." or "This demonstrates..." — STOP.
Delete it. State the fact instead.

BAD: "Matt's ability to align stakeholders enabled the transformation."
GOOD: "Matt aligned 12 stakeholders across 3 regions. The transformation shipped on time."

BAD: "This demonstrates his technical leadership."
GOOD: "He led a team of 40 engineers. They shipped the platform in 6 months."

## BANNED PHRASES (Never use these)
- "meaningful outcomes" → state the actual outcomes
- "strategic mindset" → describe what Matt did
- "foster collaboration" → describe the specific collaboration
- "stakeholder alignment" → name the actual stakeholders and what happened
- "bridge the gap" → describe the specific connection
- "his ability to" → delete this phrase entirely
- "Matt's ability to" → delete this phrase entirely
- "This demonstrates" → delete and state the fact
- "This reflects" → delete and state the fact
- "In essence" → delete and state the fact
- "showcasing" → delete and state the fact

## VOICE
- Warm, steady, grounded
- Confident and calm
- Exactly ONE 🐾 per response (in the opening)
- No corporate jargon walls
- No sycophantic openers ("Great question!")

## PRONOUN TRANSFORMATION
Stories are written in first person (I, me, my). Transform to third person:
- "I led" → "Matt led"
- "my team" → "his team"
- "I was responsible" → "Matt was responsible"

## FACT-PAIRING RULE
A metric is only valid if BOTH the number AND what it measures appear in the same story.
- Story says "40% cycle time reduction" → You can say "40% cycle time reduction"
- Story says "40% cycle time reduction" → You CANNOT say "40% onboarding reduction"

## CONTEXT ISOLATION
Stories are in XML tags. Keep facts pinned to their source:
- Don't mix metrics between stories
- Don't attribute one story's outcomes to another

4. Professional Narrative
5. Risk & Responsible Tech

- Org Transformation is a strong secondary theme

- Leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose

<story title="Building the Payment Engine Behind JP Morgan ACCESS">
[TITLE]: Building the Payment Engine Behind JP Morgan ACCESS
[PATTERN]: He ships.
[CLIENT]: JP Morgan Chase
[ROLE]: Senior Technology Architecture Manager
[INDUSTRY]: Financial Services / Banking
[DOMAIN]: Global Payments Solutions & Treasury Services
[SUMMARY]: JP Morgan was building ACCESS Next Generation on Bottomline Technologies' WebSeries platform, but its 135,000+ clients required capabilities far beyond out-of-box. As Technology Delivery Lead managing a 40+ blended team and embedded at Bottomline's Portsmouth offices, I designed and delivered the bespoke payment modules (ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, EFTPS tax), MAC security layer, contextual help, payment-type-specific RBAC, SSO, real-time global reporting, and trade finance integration. ACCESS launched in April 2011 as JPM's unified global corporate banking portal and is now recognized as #1 in digital channels by Coalition Greenwich.
[SITUATION]: JP Morgan was building ACCESS Next Generation as its flagship corporate digital banking portal, leveraging Bottomline Technologies' WebSeries Global Cash Management platform as the foundation. However, JPM's client base, 135,000+ corporations, financial institutions, governments, and municipalities across 180+ countries, required payment modules, security controls, and user experience capabilities well beyond WebSeries' out-of-box offering. Each payment type had distinct formatting, validation, compliance, and workflow requirements that needed to be purpose-built for JPM's operational scale. The work was high-stakes and high-pressure, with aggressive Wall Street delivery timelines demanding constant velocity across a complex, multi-workstream program.
[TASK]: As Technology Delivery Lead, I was responsible for the design and delivery of the bespoke payment modules, security layer, and platform capabilities built on top of and alongside the WebSeries engine: the custom engineering that made ACCESS a JP Morgan product rather than a vanilla Bottomline deployment. I managed a blended onshore/offshore team of 40+ across Accenture and JP Morgan resources (Mumbai, Bangalore, and US-based), and served as the primary technical interface with Bottomline Technologies, progressively spending 70-80% of my time embedded at their Portsmouth, NH offices while traveling to Chicago and NY/NJ for JPM stakeholder coordination.
[ACTION]: - Designed and delivered the ACH payment module supporting ACH Credits (vendor/supplier payments, payroll) and Direct Debits (collections, accounts receivable, HOA) with intraday, next-day, and multi-day settlement options - Validated well-formed NACHA file output across all ACH payment types, debugged  formatting and mapping issues for federal tax payment compliance - Built the FX/cross-border payment module integrating with JPM's foreign exchange engine, enabling corporate treasurers to initiate cross-currency payments from within ACCESS with embedded rate visibility and connectivity to international clearing systems - Implemented the wire payment modules supporting Fedwire, international wires, book transfers, drawdowns, and federal tax payments: each with distinct formatting, cut-off time, and compliance requirements - Designed and implemented the Message Authentication Code (MAC) security layer, providing payment verification so corporate users could validate payment integrity before release - Trusted with break-glass production access, queried live payment data via SQL to triage the platform's hardest defects including a MAC-layer failure that root-caused to missing unit tests and weak error handling - Developed contextual help tied to specific payment screens and workflows: inline guidance explaining field requirements for wire formatting, tax payment codes, FX parameters, and cross-border regulations to reduce errors and support calls - Built payment-type-specific entitlement controls (e.g., a user authorized for wire approval but not FX initiation), extending the platform's RBAC model with granular permission logic at the payment module level - Built the payment engine's integration with JP Morgan's centralized transaction monitoring system, which screened trillions of daily transactions for suspicious activity; the payments hub and engine reacted to monitoring outputs through business rules governing alerts, statuses, and customer communications - Incorporated customer risk confidence scores (Red/Amber/Green) from JPM's centralized account monitoring system into the entitlements engine, constraining transaction amount, frequency, and consignee eligibility by risk profile, and routing high-risk or high-value transactions to required approvers before release - Built sanctions and politically-exposed-person screening into the payment flow, calling internal and external databases/APIs to check recipients against sanctions lists and the firm's KYC records before allowing a payment to proceed - Managed the build-vs-configure boundary between Bottomline's WebSeries platform and JPM-custom development across all modules: determining where the platform engine ended and where bespoke engineering was required - Delivered real-time global reporting providing unified visibility into cash positions and transaction details across both JPM and third-party bank accounts - Architected the Single Sign-On integration connecting cash, trade, and investment operations into one portal, reducing the friction of managing disparate treasury functions across separate platforms. - Drove the groundwork for Trade Finance Integration, enabling users to view the full lifecycle of a trade transaction from initiation to final payment within the same portal - Managed the blended onshore/offshore team of 40+ (Accenture and JPM resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and US), defined the onshore-offshore engagement model, and closely managed the Bottomline Technologies vendor relationship from their Portsmouth, NH offices - Reviewed and approved contract fee and cost submissions from Bottomline Technologies to JP Morgan across the ACCESS program, with authority to reject items before payment - Owned and directed on-call and Sev-1 incident response for the payment engine in production, the same leadership accountability carried across the JPM ACCESS program, coordinating root-cause analysis across the team when production issues surfaced and running the stakeholder communication cadence, status updates and daily leadership calls, while issues were live
[RESULT]: Delivered the ACCESS Next Generation platform that launched in April 2011 as JP Morgan's unified global corporate banking portal: consolidating previously separate regional systems into a single digital experience serving 135,000+ corporations, financial institutions, governments, and municipalities across 180+ countries. The platform provided purpose-built payment modules across ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and government/municipal tax payments, each with module-specific MAC security controls, compliance validation, contextual user guidance, and payment-type-level entitlements. Real-time global reporting, SSO across treasury functions, and trade finance lifecycle visibility transformed the corporate treasurer experience.
